2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 "Products" means whole frozen chickens, chicken portions, and chicken offal as
specified in Schedule A.

2.2 "Delivery Point" means the Buyer's central kitchen at 3 Ogunlana Drive, Surulere,
Lagos, or such other location as the Buyer may designate in writing at least
forty-eight (48) hours in advance.

2.3 "Business Day" means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays in Lagos State.

2.4 "Force Majeure" has the meaning set out in Clause 11.

---

3. TERM

3.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for a period of
twelve (12) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 12.

3.2 Either party may propose renewal of this Agreement in writing not less than sixty
(60) days before expiry. Any renewal shall be subject to renegotiation of pricing
and volumes.

3.3 No auto-renewal shall apply. Should the parties continue to act as if the
Agreement is in force after expiry without a signed renewal, the terms of this
Agreement shall govern such continued performance on a month-to-month basis.

---

4. PRODUCTS AND QUALITY STANDARDS

4.1 The Supplier shall supply Products that conform to the specifications in Schedule
A, including weight ranges, packaging, and labelling.

4.2 All Products must be fit for human consumption, sourced from facilities
registered with the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
(NAFDAC), and comply with the Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency standards.

4.3 The Supplier warrants that Products shall be free from:
   (a) antibiotics or growth hormones in excess of permitted limits;
   (b) artificial colouring or preservatives not declared on the label;
   (c) any defect that renders them unwholesome or unfit for human consumption.

4.4 The Buyer may, at its own cost, conduct random laboratory testing of delivered
Products. If a test reveals non-conformity, the cost of testing shall be borne by
the Supplier and the Buyer may reject the entire relevant delivery.

4.5 Rejected Products shall be removed by the Supplier within twenty-four (24) hours
of written notice at the Supplier's cost. Failure to remove shall entitle the
Buyer to dispose of them and charge the Supplier for disposal costs.

---

5. DELIVERY SCHEDULE

5.1 The Supplier shall deliver Products according to the weekly schedule set out in
Schedule B, or as otherwise agreed in writing between the parties.

5.2 Standard delivery windows are:
   (a) Monday to Friday: 06:00 – 10:00 hours;
   (b) Saturday: 06:00 – 09:00 hours;
   (c) Sundays and public holidays: no standard deliveries, unless agreed in
       advance.

5.3 The Buyer shall provide a purchase order at least seventy-two (72) hours before
the required delivery date. The Supplier shall confirm acceptance within
twenty-four (24) hours of receipt.

5.4 Time is of the essence for deliveries to the Buyer's central kitchen. Any
delivery more than two (2) hours late without prior notice may be refused.

5.5 Partial deliveries are permitted only with the Buyer's prior written consent.
Shortfalls in any delivery shall be made up within forty-eight (48) hours.

5.6 The Supplier shall provide delivery dockets showing the Agreement number,
product code, weight, and date. The Buyer's receiving officer shall sign the
docket as proof of delivery; such signature does not constitute acceptance of
quality or quantity.

---

6. PRICE AND PAYMENT

6.1 The prices for Products are set out in Schedule A and are fixed for the first
six (6) months of the term. Thereafter, prices may be reviewed quarterly by
mutual written agreement.

6.2 All prices are in Nigerian Naira (NGN) and are exclusive of Value Added Tax
(VAT), which shall be added at the prevailing rate.

6.3 The Buyer shall pay invoices within thirty (30) days of the end of the month in
which the relevant delivery was made. Payment shall be by bank transfer to the
Supplier's designated account.

(a) the other party commits a material breach of any provision of this

       over any of its assets.

9.2 The Buyer may terminate this Agreement by giving the Supplier not less
than thirty (30) days written notice, for any reason or no reason.

than sixty (60) days written notice, provided that such notice shall not
be given during the first six (6) months of the Term.

9.4 Upon termination for any reason, the Buyer shall pay for all Products
delivered and accepted up to the date of termination, in accordance with
clause 6.3.

9.5 Clauses which by their nature are intended to survive termination shall

confidentiality, limitation of liability, and dispute resolution.

---

11. FORCE MAJEURE

11.1 Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its
    obligations under this Agreement if such failure or delay results from
    a force majeure event, including but not limited to: acts of God,
    fire, flood, storm, earthquake, epidemic, pandemic, government
    restrictions, strikes, lockouts, or any other event beyond the
    reasonable control of the affected party.

11.2 The affected party shall notify the other party in writing within
    seventy-two (72) hours of the occurrence of a force majeure event,
    stating the nature of the event and its estimated duration.

11.3 If a force majeure event continues for more than thirty (30) days,
    either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, without
    liability.

11.4 The Supplier shall not be entitled to rely on force majeure where the
    event could have been avoided by reasonable precautions or where the
    Supplier has failed to take reasonable steps to mitigate the effects
    of the event.

8.4.3 If the Supplier is unable to meet a scheduled delivery date for any reason other than a Force Majeure Event, the Supplier shall notify the Buyer as soon as reasonably practicable and shall use reasonable endeavours to agree an alternative delivery date with the Buyer.

**8.5 Minimum Monthly Quantity**

8.5.1 Subject to clause 8.3.3, the Buyer shall purchase, and the Supplier shall supply, a minimum monthly quantity of Poultry Products of five thousand kilograms (5,000 kg) in each calendar month during the Term, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

8.5.2 The minimum monthly quantity shall be measured on the basis of the quantity of Poultry Products actually delivered and accepted under this Agreement in the relevant calendar month, excluding any quantity rejected in accordance with clause 8.2.2.

8.5.3 The parties acknowledge that the minimum monthly quantity is based on the Buyer's historical purchasing patterns and forecast demand. The Buyer may request a review of the minimum monthly quantity if its operational requirements change materially, and the parties shall discuss any such request in good faith.

**8.6 Shortfall**

8.6.1 If, in any calendar month, the total quantity of Poultry Products delivered and accepted under this Agreement is less than the minimum monthly quantity, the Buyer shall pay to the Supplier, within thirty (30) days of the end of the relevant calendar month, an amount equal to the difference between the minimum monthly quantity and the quantity actually delivered and accepted, multiplied by the Unit Price. This amount is referred to in this Agreement as the "Shortfall Payment".
**8.7 Payment of Shortfall Payment**

8.7.1 The Shortfall Payment shall be calculated and invoiced by the Supplier on a monthly basis. The Supplier shall issue an invoice for the Shortfall Payment, if any, within fourteen (14) days of the end of the relevant calendar month, together with a statement showing the calculation of the Shortfall Payment in reasonable detail.

8.7.2 The Buyer shall pay the Shortfall Payment within thirty (30) days of receipt of the relevant invoice, in accordance with the payment terms set out in clause 7.

8.7.3 The parties may agree in writing to offset the Shortfall Payment against any amounts owed by the Supplier to the Buyer under this Agreement or any other agreement between the parties.

8.7.4 For the avoidance of doubt, the payment of a Shortfall Payment shall not relieve the Buyer of its obligation to purchase the minimum monthly quantity in subsequent months, and the Shortfall Payment shall not be credited against any future delivery of Poultry Products.

2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 "Products" means whole frozen chickens, chicken portions, and chicken offal as
specified in Schedule A.

2.2 "Delivery Point" means the Buyer's central kitchen at 3 Ogunlana Drive, Surulere,
Lagos, or such other location as the Buyer may designate in writing at least
forty-eight (48) hours in advance.

2.3 "Business Day" means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays in Lagos State.

2.4 "Force Majeure" has the meaning set out in Clause 11.

---

3. TERM

3.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for a period of
twelve (12) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 12.

3.2 Either party may propose renewal of this Agreement in writing not less than sixty
(60) days before expiry. Any renewal shall be subject to renegotiation of pricing
and volumes.

3.3 No auto-renewal shall apply. Should the parties continue to act as if the
Agreement is in force after expiry without a signed renewal, the terms of this
Agreement shall govern such continued performance on a month-to-month basis.

---

4. PRODUCTS AND QUALITY STANDARDS

4.1 The Supplier shall supply Products that conform to the specifications in Schedule
A, including weight ranges, packaging, and labelling.

4.2 All Products must be fit for human consumption, sourced from facilities
registered with the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
(NAFDAC), and comply with the Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency standards.

4.3 The Supplier warrants that Products shall be free from:
   (a) antibiotics or growth hormones in excess of permitted limits;
   (b) artificial colouring or preservatives not declared on the label;
   (c) any defect that renders them unwholesome or unfit for human consumption.

The contract start_date for Sunshine Contract #SC-2021-014 is 2021-03-01. Record status: historical.

4.4 The Buyer may, at its own cost, conduct random laboratory testing of delivered
Products. If a test reveals non-conformity, the cost of testing shall be borne by
the Supplier and the Buyer may reject the entire relevant delivery.

4.5 Rejected Products shall be removed by the Supplier within twenty-four (24) hours
of written notice at the Supplier's cost. Failure to remove shall entitle the
Buyer to dispose of them and charge the Supplier for disposal costs.

---

5. DELIVERY SCHEDULE

5.1 The Supplier shall deliver Products according to the weekly schedule set out in
Schedule B, or as otherwise agreed in writing between the parties.

5.2 Standard delivery windows are:
   (a) Monday to Friday: 06:00 – 10:00 hours;
   (b) Saturday: 06:00 – 09:00 hours;
   (c) Sundays and public holidays: no standard deliveries, unless agreed in
       advance.

5.3 The Buyer shall provide a purchase order at least seventy-two (72) hours before
the required delivery date. The Supplier shall confirm acceptance within
twenty-four (24) hours of receipt.

5.4 Time is of the essence for deliveries to the Buyer's central kitchen. Any
delivery more than two (2) hours late without prior notice may be refused.

5.5 Partial deliveries are permitted only with the Buyer's prior written consent.
Shortfalls in any delivery shall be made up within forty-eight (48) hours.

5.6 The Supplier shall provide delivery dockets showing the Agreement number,
product code, weight, and date. The Buyer's receiving officer shall sign the
docket as proof of delivery; such signature does not constitute acceptance of
quality or quantity.

---

6. PRICE AND PAYMENT

6.1 The prices for Products are set out in Schedule A and are fixed for the first
six (6) months of the term. Thereafter, prices may be reviewed quarterly by
mutual written agreement.

6.2 All prices are in Nigerian Naira (NGN) and are exclusive of Value Added Tax
(VAT), which shall be added at the prevailing rate.

6.3 The Buyer shall pay invoices within thirty (30) days of the end of the month in
which the relevant delivery was made. Payment shall be by bank transfer to the
Supplier's designated account.

5.2.2 Upon the expiry of the initial term, and at any time thereafter, either party may propose a review of the Unit Price by giving not less than thirty (30) days' written notice to the other party. 5.3.2 The volume discount shall be calculated on the basis of the historical Unit Price set out in clause 5.1 for the relevant period, and shall be shown as a separate line item on the monthly statement of account.

5.3.3 For the avoidance of doubt, the volume discount is not a reduction in the Unit Price itself but a credit calculated on the value of the delivered quantity in the relevant month. ------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY 014-04
Date: 2021-08-09
Parties: LKC Quality Control (M. Ade) / Sunshine Poultry Ltd (production manager)
Issue summary: Quality complaint — high incidence of bruised carcasses in 3 deliveries (2–6 Aug).
Proposed change: Request for replacement product on affected lots; also request for Sunshine to implement on-line inspection step.
Negotiation note: Sunshine disputed extent of bruising but offered 5% credit on those invoices. QC rejected, wanted 10%. Sunshine held at 7.5% credit. QC accepted. Inspection step: Sunshine said they already do visual check; agreed to add a second check at the packing table. No formal CR.
Status: CLOSED — credit applied on invoice nos. SP-2204, SP-2211, SP-2218. Inspection note confirmed 2021-08-15.

------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY 014-05
Date: 2021-10-30
Parties: LKC Procurement (A. Okafor) / Sunshine Poultry Ltd (S. Adeyemi)
Issue summary: Delivery schedule change request (permanent) — reduce weekly volume from 4,500 kg to 4,000 kg.
Proposed change: Volume reduction due to LKC outlet closure in Surulere.
Negotiation note: Sunshine resisted — said their production planning was set for 4,500 kg. Asked LKC to keep volume for another 8 weeks. LKC said they could not. Both sides agreed to a 6-week transition: 4,300 kg for Nov, 4,100 kg for Dec, then 4,000 kg from Jan 2022.
Status: CLOSED — agreed via email 2021-11-05.

------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY 014-06
Date: 2022-01-14
Parties: LKC Procurement (T. Bello) / Sunshine Poultry Ltd (S. Adeyemi)
Issue summary: Price adjustment request (second) — Sunshine seeking NGN 2,250/kg for Q2 2022.
Proposed change: Increase effective 2022-04-01.

2. MANAGING DIRECTOR'S REPORT ON OPERATIONS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE — Q1 2022

Mrs. Adaeze Okafor presented the operational and financial report for the first quarter of 2022 (January – March). She highlighted the following key points:

- Revenue for Q1 2022 stood at NGN 142.6 million, representing a 12.4% increase compared to Q1 2021 (NGN 126.9 million).
- Gross profit margin improved to 38.2%, up from 35.7% in the prior year quarter, driven by better procurement pricing and reduced wastage in the central kitchen.
- Operating expenses increased by 8.1% to NGN 41.8 million, mainly due to higher diesel costs for generators and a one-off repair of the cold room compressor at the Victoria Island branch.
- Net profit after tax for the quarter was NGN 18.4 million, compared to NGN 15.2 million in Q1 2021.

The MD noted that the company's cash position remained healthy at NGN 23.9 million as at 15th March 2022, with undrawn facilities of NGN 30 million on the Access Bank overdraft line.

The Board commended the MD and her team for the strong start to the year. Mrs. Ngozi Eze asked whether the improved gross margin was sustainable, and the MD explained that the procurement team had locked in fixed-price contracts with two major poultry suppliers for the first half of the year, which would protect margins even if feed costs rose.

---

3. APPROVAL OF THE IKEJA BRANCH CATERING AND SUPPLY CONTRACT

Adaeze Okafor approval_of_ikeja_contract is 2022-03-20. Record status: historical.

The MD presented a proposal for a significant new contract with a corporate client for the supply of daily meals to their staff cafeteria in Ikeja. The client, a multinational logistics company with approximately 450 employees on site, had approached LKC in January 2022 following a competitive tender process.

Key terms of the proposed contract were as follows:

- Contract duration: 24 months, renewable by mutual agreement.
- Estimated annual value: NGN 96 million (NGN 8 million per month).
- Service scope: Provision of breakfast and lunch on weekdays, plus special catering for corporate events (estimated 4–6 events per year).
- Staffing requirement: 14 additional kitchen and service staff, to be recruited and trained by LKC.
- Equipment and infrastructure: The client would provide the kitchen space and basic equipment at their Ikeja facility. LKC would be responsible for small wares, uniforms, and food safety certification for the site.
- Payment terms: 30 days from invoice, with a 10% mobilization advance upon signing.

The MD explained that the contract would require an initial capital outlay of approximately NGN 8.5 million for equipment, recruitment, and the first two months of working capital. She projected that the contract would break even by month 5 and contribute net profit of NGN 1.2 million per month from month 6 onward.

Mrs. Folake Adeyemi raised a question about the client's creditworthiness and payment history. The Legal Counsel, Mr. Femi Adewale, confirmed that due diligence had been completed, including credit checks and references from two other vendors supplying the client at other locations. Payment performance was reported to be consistent, with no history of late payments beyond 45 days.

Alhaji Musa Garba asked about the exit clause and penalties. The MD confirmed that the contract included a 90-day notice period for either party, and liquidated damages of 5% of the monthly fee in the event of service failure. She also noted that the client had requested a performance bond of NGN 5 million, which LKC would procure from a reputable insurance company at an estimated cost of NGN 150,000 per year.

Discussion followed on the capacity of the existing central kitchen to handle the additional volume. The Head of Operations, Mrs. Bisi Johnson, was invited to speak to this item. She reported that the central kitchen had idle capacity of roughly 30% and could absorb the additional production without major capital expenditure. However, she recommended a phased ramp-up: starting with breakfast-only service for the first two weeks, then adding lunch once the new staff were fully trained.

The improvement was attributed to better procurement practices, reduced food wastage, and the higher-margin catering contracts secured during the year.
